The question asks what is more plausible in Finland than elsewhere based on the data in the passage.  
The passage emphasizes that sauna use is much more common in Finland and links frequent sauna use to health benefits such as reduced cardiovascular mortality, reduced dementia risk, and reduced all-cause mortality.  

- (A) More gold medals in adolescent skiing — not supported by the passage; skiing is unrelated to sauna data.  
- (B) An 86-year old male mayor revered in the community — possible but not directly tied to sauna use data; longevity is mentioned, but specific revered status is speculative.  
- (C) Increased rate of pets in the household — no connection to sauna use or Finnish population data in the passage.  
- (D) Improved marriage satisfaction rates — not mentioned in the passage; no data linking sauna use to marriage satisfaction.  

However, the passage does show that frequent sauna use is linked to longevity and reduced dementia.  
If sauna use is much more common in Finland, then it’s plausible that Finland has more very old, healthy individuals compared to other countries.  
Option (B) — an 86-year-old male mayor revered in the community — fits with the idea of more old people in good health (due to frequent sauna use) being capable of holding public office and being respected.  

Final answer: (B)
